To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1-Aminocylopropane- 1-carboxy acid (ACC), the immediate precursor of ethylene, is not a potent abscission agent in olive, and ethylene-releasing compounds, such as ethephon, are effective abscission agents in olive, and the timing of the application of these compounds in relation to anthesis is critical to the success of the treatment.

1) the ethylene-releasing agent ethephon (ET) induces abscission of leaves in olive shoots in vitro; 2) the burst of ethylene evolution caused by the ethylene precursor ACC does not induce abscissision; 3) the duration of ethylen evolution is critical in abscission induction; and 4) the duration of ET-induced ethylene evolution is longer in reproductive than in vegetative shoots.
ethylene is a major abscissic hormone for olive, but that it is not released in a single burst but rather over a long period of time.

the role of ethylene in the abscission of olive leaves in vitro.
the role of ethylene as a possible abscission agent in an in vitro olive shoot system.
